zones.label: Column 1 running header
zones.note: The small upper-margin ink blemish was misrecognized as a numeral 2; no printed text is transcribed for that mark.

lines.note: Gojuracu aru and the honorific alternative nasaruru continue the preceding entry: a dignitary's entry into the capital. The initial I/J convention elsewhere on this page does not alter the printed G here.

runs.text: o Cubǒſama, ou outra peßoa grande como o ſe-

lines.note: The Portuguese names Cubosama and another great person as subjects of entrar. The abraded title is read Cubǒſama from the surviving letters and mark; its b and vowel accent remain less secure than the surrounding gloss.
Completes senhor and locates the ruler's entry in Miyaco, the capital. Tenca and Miyaco are Japanese designations inside Portuguese prose; the OCR's Mõyaco is not supported by the visible y.
Juraku is independently glossed as a place of many pleasures. It should not be conflated structurally with the honorific arrival example ending immediately above.
Jurai is explained by iri kitaru, coming in or arriving. The initial is capital I, not long s; Portuguese vinda confirms that this is an arrival noun.
The distinct long-vowel headword juurai means from then until now. Preserve its visible mark and the Portuguese grave accent in atè rather than merging it with the preceding jurai.
Juurin is trampling, explained by fumi nijiru and Portuguese pisar com os pès. The damaged headword begins Iǔ, not the OCR's Fh; the next example repeats the same word.
Hito wo juurin suru means trampling or kicking someone. The Portuguese dar continues into lhe couces on the next physical line.

The opening phrase completes 'give him kicks'. The following compound describes forcibly or deceitfully taking someone along. Second-pass inspection supports côin with a circumflex and final in, rather than the OCR's côm.

runs.text: guem por força, ou enganado dando lhe de

lines.note: Guem completes alguem. The gloss specifies force or deception together with kicking, continuing the explanation introduced by Iǔrin, côin.
Couces completes the kicking expression. Final upright S. is the dictionary's written-usage label, not part of the italic Portuguese sentence.
Jurin, paraphrased as hayashi, means a wood or grove. This short-vowel noun is distinct from juurin above; the final S. marks written usage.
Juryoo is explained as kuni na, names derived from provinces or realms. The scan separates Cuni and na; the explanatory i, and the headword's caron are preserved.
The gloss describes adopting such names as titles. Kai no kami and the divided fi- begin examples; the lower-case fi- must remain attached physically to this row.
Fi- plus jenno gives Hizen no kami. Juryoo serareta illustrates receiving such a provincial title; the scan supports xerareta, not OCR xetareta, and retains the i before the accented o.

runs.text: Ser poſto a alguem eſte nome de reino.

lines.note: The Portuguese translates the preceding passive/honorific example as having this provincial designation bestowed on someone. It does not introduce another headword.
Juurui is a following or household of servants, paraphrased as shitagoo tagui. Preserve the distinct vowel marks and the printed final y in taguy.
Juurui kenzoku expands the reference to servants and household dependants. The Portuguese list continues below with relatives and people attached to a house.

runs.text: de parentes remotos, ou gente que pertẽce a al-

lines.note: The definition includes distant relatives and people belonging to a household. The tilde in pertẽce abbreviates the nasal consonant; al- continues on the next line.
Gũa completes algũa from the preceding row: people attached to some household. This short continuation remains an independent physical line.
Jusan means gathering and dispersing, paraphrased by atsumari chiru. The scan supplies a word space between the Japanese verbs; no hyphen is added after the visibly unhyphenated espa.
Lharse completes espalharse. The Japanese example concerns gathering, dispersing and change as conditions of worldly life; xe- continues into jǒno below.
Sejoo no arisama nari completes the statement about the world's condition. The Portuguese begins with capital O, not OCR G, and repeats gathering and scattering.

runs.text: & mudarſe he maneira, & cuſtume do mũdo.

lines.note: Changing, as well as gathering and dispersing, is described as the way and custom of the world. The printed abbreviated mũdo is not expanded.
Juusoku denotes being full, paraphrased by michi fusagaru. De- begins Deus inside the Japanese example on the following row; it is not the beginning of the Portuguese translation yet.

runs.text: us izzucunimo jǔſocu xi maximaſu. D

lines.note: Deus izzucu ni mo juusoku shi mashimasu states that God is fully present everywhere. The second De- is italic and begins Portuguese Deos, whose remaining os occupies the next row.

runs.text: os eſtà plenariamente em toda a parte.

lines.note: Os completes Deos across the physical line break, followed by 'is fully present everywhere'. Removing the OCR's duplicated De preserves the actual division rather than joining the word editorially.
Jussaku denotes composition, paraphrased by nobe tsukuru. The first gloss concerns composing long Chinese verses; ver- is the visible beginning of versos across the break.

runs.text: ſos da China compridos. ¶ Item, Compor

lines.note: Sos completes versos, specified as long Chinese verse. Item introduces the broader sense of composing books rather than a new Japanese headword.
Livros completes the broader composition gloss. The final upright S. identifies written usage and is kept separate from the italic apparatus.

Jut, corresponding to jutsu, is glossed as a wonder or apparent miracle. Apparente is the dictionary's qualification; the final bare t is the historical checked-coda spelling, not a missing syllable to supply.
Majut illustrates a magical art or apparent wonder. The visible initial paragraph mark was missing from the OCR and is restored on this same physical line.

runs.text: do Diabo. ¶ Item, Meo, ou remedio. Vt,

lines.note: Do Diabo completes the dictionary's religious characterization of majut. A further sense of jut is a means or remedy, leading into the negative example below.
Jutnai is something troublesome and without remedy. The upright n is visible; OCR Iuthai would obscure the negative adjective repeated as a separate headword below.

runs.text: Arte, ou meo, ou marauilha. S.

lines.note: Jutdoo denotes an art, means, or wonder, continuing the vocabulary of techniques and remedies. Capital I and the caron over o are visible; S. is a written-usage label.
Jutji is assigned the same meanings as Iutdǒ by Idem. This complete but short entry is not a continuation of the preceding Portuguese sentence.
Jutnai now receives its own entry, describing something painful, troublesome and without remedy. The scan supports tn, not the OCR's rm sequence.
Remedio completes sem remedio in the preceding definition. The following two indented forms derive from this adjective rather than continuing the Portuguese gloss.
Jutnasa is the nominal form expressing the troublesome or distressing quality described above. No Portuguese gloss is printed on this row, so none is supplied in the transcription.
Jutnoo is the corresponding contracted adverbial form. Its marked long vowel belongs to the printed inflection, and the row remains separate from the next headword.

runs.text: Certa ſeita da china que enſina a viuer bẽ

lines.note: Jutoo refers here to a Chinese moral teaching or school. The scan restores Certa seita and ensina a; the tightly printed viuerbẽ is retained without silently expanding the nasal abbreviation.
Moralmente completes the description of teaching people to live well morally. It belongs to the doctrinal entry, not the tree-top noun that follows.

runs.text: Põtas altas dos raminhos das aruores. S

lines.note: This differently marked jutoo denotes the upper tips of tree branches. The Portuguese begins Põtas, with an abbreviation tilde over o, not OCR Pitas; the circumflex contrasts with Iutǒ above.
Juuoo is explained by tate yoko, lengthwise and crosswise. The capital I and the two vowel marks replace the OCR's malformed initial without modernizing the romanization.
Juuoo jizai ni kake meguru describes moving freely in every direction. The visible spacing caqem eguru is retained as a diplomatic feature; it is not interpreted as a different verb.

runs.text: cà pera là a ſua vontade, & liuremente.

lines.note: The Portuguese completes andar de: going here and there at one's own will and freely. The grave accents on cà and là are preserved independently.

runs.text: Eſcriuão, & juiz do inferno q̃ eſcreue, &

lines.note: The homographic juuoo now concerns an underworld judge and recorder. The gloss continues in column 2; q̃ abbreviates que, and the clear eſcreue replaces severely garbled OCR without inventing additional text.

runs.text: inquire dos peccados, ſegundo a opinião dos

lines.note: Continues the underworld official's actions: writing and investigating sins, according to the belief attributed by the dictionary to non-Christians. The printed verb is inquire, not imquire.
Gentios completes the source's attribution of this belief. It is the end of the Iǔuǒ gloss carried over from column 1, not a separate entry.

runs.text: Homem daquella ſeita de hũs certos Phi-

lines.note: Jusha is a member of the school of moral philosophers described below. Phi- begins Philosophos across the physical line break; the abbreviation hũs is retained.
Completes Philosophos moraes da China, Chinese moral philosophers. This defines the person belonging to the school rather than the school itself.
Jushi, paraphrased as ki no eda, means a tree branch. Upright S. is the written-usage label; the Japanese paraphrase is not an embedded term in Portuguese.
The homographic verb jushi, jusuru, jushita is equated with yomu, to read. Capital I replaces OCR lowercase l; Do- starts the following dokuju example.
Do- plus cuju forms dokuju suru, likewise reading or reciting. Idem refers to Ler above, and the word division is kept at its printed location.
Jushoo is explained by ki no kozue, the topmost small ends of branches. Preserve the circumflex in the headword and the historical spelling cozuye.
The branch tips are explicitly those of trees. This continuation closes the botanical gloss and its final written-usage label.
Juei, paraphrased by ki no kage, is the shade or shadow of a tree. The gloss is complete on this row, with no additional material supplied.

runs.text: Feſta, ou alegria que ſe faz a algum

lines.note: Juen denotes a celebration held for someone. The next rows specify the recipient as a Buddhist cleric taking up a superior's office.

runs.text: Bonzo quando o fazem ſuperior, & toma poſ

lines.note: The celebration marks a bonze being made superior and taking possession of the designated house. Preserve the unhyphenated pos at the physical edge rather than completing posse here.

runs.text: ſe da caſa determinada pera eſte officio.

lines.note: Se completes posse across the line break. The house is assigned to the office, which explains the institutional rather than merely domestic sense of the celebration.
Juyoo is accepting and using or valuing something, paraphrased as uke mochiiru. The scan supports mochijru, including the r, rather than OCR mochijiu; rece- begins recebendo.

runs.text: bendo eſtimar como vida que Deos daa, ley, ou

lines.note: Completes recebendo and explains valuing what is received, such as God-given life or a law. These are examples in the Portuguese apparatus, not further Japanese headwords.
Advice from some person completes the list of things to receive and value. Preserve the tilde carrier in dalgũa and the printed s-types.
Juyo contrasts with juyoo above: sazuke atayuru means bestowing or giving. The headword has no vowel mark in this occurrence, and the Portuguese verb begins its explanation.
The giving concerns holy things, with law or teaching as an example. The historical spelling sanctas remains unchanged.

runs.text: Criado, ou miniſtro que ajuda nos autos,

lines.note: Juuza denotes an attendant or assistant in performances. The capital I and marked u replace the OCR's lower-case initial; the specific performance types continue below.

runs.text: farſas, ou bailos ao principal autor. ¶ Itẽ,

lines.note: The assistant helps the principal performer in plays, farces or dances. Itẽ introduces an extended application rather than another literal theatrical definition.
The figurative compound juuzamuko names a man married to someone's maidservant. This occurrence visibly uses a circumflex on u, unlike the main headword's caron; preserve the distinction.
The maidservant is somebody else's employee or dependant. This completes the definition of Iûzamuco rather than the preceding theatrical sense.
Juzu denotes Buddhist prayer beads, described in the dictionary's own religious terminology. The example begins juzu wo tsu- and continues on the next physical row.
Tsumaguru and the alternative kuru mean passing the beads through the fingers. Latin l supplies 'or'; the historical Portuguese pollos is retained.
Dedos completes the first example. The second concerns rubbing prayer beads, expressed by suru or momu; unhyphenated Es begins Portuguese esfregar below.

runs.text: fregar as contas entre as mãos adorando.

lines.note: Completes esfregar: rubbing the beads between one's hands while worshipping. The tilde is visibly on a in mãos and is not moved by normalization.

runs.text: Caſa onde fazem, ou vendem contas.

lines.note: Juzuya is a place where prayer beads are made or sold. This is the last body entry before the new alphabetical M section.

Ma, equated here with tengu and glossed Diabo, begins the new section. Its M is the decorated initial spanning six physical rows; restoring it prevents the OCR's isolated A from becoming a false headword.
This ma is hemp, equated with asa. The entry is set beside the decorated M but does not inherit that letter; final S. is upright written-usage apparatus.
A third ma is explained by migaku, polishing. The Portuguese a- continues into limpar on the next row; this entry is distinct from the preceding hemp noun.
Limpar completes alimpar, to clean or polish. Ken wo masu begins an example about polishing a sword; its modal bexi follows on the next row.

Bexi completes ken wo masu beshi. The Portuguese gives a future or prescriptive translation, 'you will clean and polish the sword'. The printed space in A limparàs and its grave accent are retained; this accent differs from the acute on the following line.

The line completes the polishing translation with the sword as object. The visibly printed sacalarás and its acute accent are preserved without silently regularizing the historical spelling; S. marks written usage.
Ma now means space or room. The first example begins ma ga and continues with nai, the absence of space, on the following physical row.
Nai completes ma ga nai, there being no space. The next sense is a room, introduced by the divided Japanese term Zaxi- within the explanatory apparatus.
Qui completes Zaxiqui, paired with Portuguese camara. Ma ma ga ooi states that there are many rooms; the divided A- begins the Portuguese translation auer.

runs.text: uer muitos Zaxiquis, ou camaras, cellas, &c.

lines.note: Uer completes auer: there are many rooms or cells. The scan supports cellas rather than OCR ccllas; Zaxiquis is the Japanese-derived term embedded in the Portuguese list. The raised c at the far right belongs to &c. on this row, and the crop includes its full height.

runs.text: ¶ Item, Largura do Zaxiqui, ou camara.

lines.note: A further sense concerns the width of the room. The scan has capital Z in Zaxiqui, and the Japanese term occurs inside an otherwise Portuguese explanation.
Ma ga hiroi or sebai describes a room as broad or narrow. The second Zaxiqui is part of the Portuguese translation, whereas the preceding Japanese sentence is not an embedded typeface term.
Completes the translation as broad or narrow. The independent Ma. at the far right is a catchword anticipating the next page's Ma entry, and is represented separately as page furniture.
